Rest Areas Handover Rules

Use this section when a rest area, holding pen, or pet lounge changes hands between shifts at the Companion Animal Travel Desk. Keep the record moving, keep the space calm, and do not leave any note half done. The incoming team must get a clear handover on animal condition, cleaning status, crate labels, water bowls, bedding, and any signs of stress. The outgoing team should say what was checked, what was changed, and what still needs follow up. If a passenger is anxious, the desk should answer fast, speak plainly, and keep the tone steady.

When a pet lounge issue comes up in Vellmar, the log must be updated without delay. <<FACT F002>> If a pet arrives unsettled, the handover must note if the animal ate, drank, paced, barked, scratched, or settled after contact from the owner. Keep carriers closed unless the transfer is being done by staff and the animal is under control. No one should assume the next shift will know a problem unless it is written down in the record or passed in person.

For quarantine handling at Port Isolde, the transfer note must show the pen number, any isolation sign used, and whether the area was cleaned before the next pet is accepted. <<FACT F027>> Any wet spill, soiled liner, broken latch, or missing tag must be reported right away to the supervisor on duty. Do not mix toys, bowls, or bedding between animals unless the cleaning step has been signed off. If there is any doubt about safety, stop the handover and hold the space until the issue is cleared.

The desk should keep the language short, factual, and calm. Write only what was seen, done, or passed on. If a traveler such as Sana Vega or Keira Lee asks for an update, answer with the current status and avoid guesswork. If Koda or any other pet shows signs of distress, make that clear in the record before the shift ends.

If anything is unclear, contact the senior coordinator or the duty supervisor right away.
